title: Issues related to initializing new instance in GDExtension/Godot modules
body:
### Tested versions

- All Godot versions from 4.3 onward.

### System information

Any from Godot 4.1 onwards

### Issue description

Godot's RefCounted and Object types extended with a Script have their own virtual method for initialization – [`init`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_object.html#class-object-private-method-init). It is being called just after the script has been attached to the Object – usually when instance is ready for use.

GDExtension exposes [`create_instance_func`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/core/extension/gdextension_interface.h#L385) instead, which doesn't fulfil this role properly.

### Purpose of user-defined init

- Accessing some Godot abstractions, most notably the [`CompositorEffect`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_compositoreffect.html#class-compositoreffect).
- Creating some side effects - one might pass reference to their Resource to some user-defined Singleton to cache it, some plugins check default settings and perform non-trivial amount of work to initialize some values.
- Accessing and modifing the Editor, for example passing new commands to EditorCommandPalette, wiring Resource to ProjectSettings signals etc.
- Instantiating other objects.
- Tracking user actions (not for telemetry but one might want to track&register all the Resources/instances related to their level editor, for example).
- Many other operations which might require cloning, passing and modifying the base instance.

Unfortunately `create_instance_func` is poorly suited for any of these tasks.

## Problems with init related to classes inheriting RefCounted

Note – all of that is reproducible with Godot modules. Refcount in `create_instance_func` is `0` both for init and postinit – increasing and decreasing it will free the instance.

```cpp
ExampleClass::ExampleClass() {
	// Advertised RefCount is 1 (in reality it is 0).
	print_line("refcount: ", get_reference_count());
	Ref<ExampleClass> a = this;
	print_line("refcount: ", get_reference_count());
	// RefCount goes from 0 to 1 - `a` is being dropped and instance is being freed.
}

ExampleClass::~ExampleClass() {
	print_line("Deconstructor.");
}
```

```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
	var example := ExampleClass.new()
	# E 0:00:00:364   _ready: Cannot call method 'print_type' on a null value.
	example.print_type(example)
```

`NOTIFICATION_POSTINITIALIZE` is being emitted by GDExtension library, inside `create_instance_func callback`, while instance is still being created (i.e. before it has been passed back to Godot) and obeys the same rules.

It is hard to say what will increase, and what will decrease the refcount, and what actions will or will not result in UB due to that.

For example, following snippet will result in instant UB for RefCounted classes in GDExtension (not tested against modules but possible):

```cpp
ExampleClass::ExampleClass() {
    bool is_nil = UtilityFunctions::is_same(this, Variant());
    UtilityFunctions::print("It seems that my instance is not nil, is it? ", is_nil);
}
```

As binding maintainers we can't say which functions are sound (i.e. won't cause UB) and which aren't (or if they are safe only every third Tuesday of the month, iff I make a function call while standing on one leg).

One can argue that extra initialization logic could be moved to the caller site – i.e. by exposing extra method or two, which would be reasonable limitation – unfortunately doing so in Editor is very hacky (because instance is being instantiated, kept, and "owned" by the Editor, not the userspace) or straight up impossible.


### Current workaround in Godot-rust

Long story short currently we use deferred refcount (you can read more about it in our [docs](https://godot-rust.github.io/docs/gdext/master/godot/prelude/struct.Base.html#method.to_init_gd)). It is not perfect hack, but covers most base cases and is sound (i.e. won't cause the UB). Unfortunately we can't say what given instance is being created for which results in janky behavior.

## Why should we bother at all 🤔?

In general patterns described in [Purpose of user-defined init](#purpose-of-user-defined-init) are pretty common for gdscript and gdextension codebases – which means that godot-dotnet will run into this issue as well. 

From our side – initialization issues are source of never-ending headaches, and no hack can address it properly and in full.

## What can be done?

1) Ideally – give us real, constructed instance in `init` and provide the flag telling us what given instance is being created for (default data? docs? real use by user?). `Bool` would be enough.
2) Leave init as it is, add another lifecycle virtual method/callback.  I'm not huge fan of that, we already have healthy abundance of virtual lifecycle methods.
3) Add  notification which would be emitted when Object is being put into use.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Create class via GDExtension or modules which anyhow increases and decreases RefCount in its constructor.
2. Try to create it


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Godot module showcasing this issue – contains two commented examples in `broken_init.cpp`, `Example 1` (constructor) and `Example 2` (notification post-initialize). Put it into `modules` folder, compile, and try to construct given instance anyhow, for example with:

```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
	var example := ExampleClass.new()
	example.print_type(example)
```

[broken_init.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22621524/broken_init.zip)

<details>
<summary> Decided as not important - user should be responsible for cleanup of their instance no matter what is the call site </summary>


## `init` being invoked for editor purposes leads to janky and/or undesired side effects

As has been mentioned earlier, `create_instance_func` is being called by the Editor for multitude of purposes (docs, default values for placeholder instances...). We can't say if given instance is going to be `memdeleted` by Godot instantly, and so can't the user.

An example of such behavior can be found here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/108614#issuecomment-3350521825. 

See: [godot rust issue](https://github.com/godot-rust/gdext/issues/1296) and [part of the Godot code responsible for memdeleting freshly created instances](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6339f31a0217038ce6ed5e16776e34654895edc6/core/object/class_db.cpp#L2220-L2240).

Initialized non-refcounted object being nil is not end of the world but it is yet another annoyance – this behaviour might be also hard to spot&debug if one is not familiar with inner workings of the engine.

</details>
